substantial.problem: The row states as fact that Liele 'was the slave of a British officer' whose 'master brought him to Kingston'. This rests on Phillippo (1843) alone, and the Library's primary, Liele's own narrative in Rippon, says the opposite: his master Henry Sharp had freed him, and he came to Jamaica as an indentured servant to pay a debt to Colonel Kirkland. substantial.problem: The claim that the Conselheiro attacked the Roman Church is contested, and the row gives one side. In Euclides it is not a report of the Conselheiro's words: it sits inside Euclides's comparison with Themison and Montanus, borrowed from Renan ('estadeiando o mesmo argumento que aquelle'). The row reorders it so the claim reads as a report and the comparison as a separate remark. The same book holds the other side, which the drafter did not use: an officer Euclides quotes says the Conselheiro promoted baptisms, marriages, feasts and novenas; and a Capuchin friar's report prints the Conselheiro's own answer that his quarrel was with the Republic. The same book also holds the institutional act that runs the other way: the archbishop of Bahia's circular of 16 February 1882 forbidding the faithful to gather to hear him, and the friar's mission of May 1895 'em nome do Sr. Arcebispo'. So the link 'Canudos argued against VIII.48' rests on an analogy, while the documented argument runs VIII.48 → Canudos. The floorNote's 'none were read' is also inexact, since the friar's report gives the Conselheiro's words, though through a hostile witness.
substantial.evidence: Euclides raw (my fetch), all verbatim: 'E* um dissidente do molde exacto de Themison. Insurge-se contra a igreja romana, e vibra-lhe objurgatorias, estadeiando o mesmo argumento que aquelle'; 'promove os baptisados, casamentos, desobrigas, festas, novenas' (Durval Vieira de Aguiar, quoted); 'Circular dirigida em 16 de Fevereiro de 1882, ao elero bahiano pelo arcebispo D. Luiz.'; '«zendo saber aos Parochianos que lhes prohibimos «absolutamente, de se reunirem para ouvir tal pré- «gação'; 'Em 1895, em certa manhã de Maio'; 'Frei João Evangelista de Monte-Marciano'; 'Por isto, de ordem, e em nome do Sr. Arcebispo ia abrir uma santa missão e acon- selhar o povo a dispersar-se e a voltar aos lares e ao trabalho'; 'No tempo da monarchia deixei-me prender porque reconhecia o governo, hoje não porque não reconheço a Republica.'

The friar reports the Conselheiro's answer. Under the monarchy, he said, he had let himself be arrested, because he recognized that government. substantial.problem: 'An army order dated 6 September 1897 still tells of shelling the church towers. Euclides says Canudos fell on the 5th, at dusk.' Judgments the task asked for. (a) VII.5 → Caribbean 'gave rise to', Inferential-Thin: it holds. Phillippo dates the Wesleyan mission to 1789 under Coke. The type fits mission planting, and the grade is the cap without a secondary read. Strengthen the row text per S6. (b) Canudos → VIII.48 'argued against': retire it, and draft VIII.48 → Canudos 'argued against' with an outcome on the 1882 circular (S2). (c) VIII.48 → Canudos 'influenced': keep it, with the stronger quotes (m5). (d) The Juazeiro hold is right. The ruling binds the drafter to the recommendation, but only V items carry a sentence. The record's Juazeiro items are [S] and a V (bib) study, and Della Cava is in copyright and unread. A line written now would be invented. 'Take every recommendation' cannot override the evidence rule or CLAUDE.md's 'never invent', so the hold, logged in Open-Gaps with its wait, is the faithful way to carry it out. (e) The VIII.41 Lutheran hold is right on the same ground: the record's only item is [S]. (f) The 1907 edition of the 1815 Inquisition papers is acceptable as it stands. The rule's cut is 'before about 1930, public domain', and 'nothing after 1906' limits the events told, not the date of an edition. The documents are of 1815. It is a source the drafter added and opened raw, which the brief allows with a flag, and the row names the court's hostility. No ruling from Mark is needed. (g) Sharpe as 'a Baptist', not 'deacon', is right: Bleby never uses the word. In Rippon, 'deacon' belongs to Henry Sharp, Liele's master, which may be where the record's word came from. (h) Canudos livingEvidence group 'ended' is right and matches P2-V precedent for crushed communities: VII.11 Antonian movement, VII.15 Camisards, VII.9 Port-Royal, VIII.44 Taiping.
